real_issues_caught: §6 chunkwise: flagged that the bare state update S_{c+1}=S_c+K_c^T V_c is the UN-GATED additive case only; DeltaNet/Mamba-2/GLA must fold the (I-βkk^T) erase / α decay factors into the intra-chunk and cross-chunk operators. The tutorial already scoped §6 to '以无门控线性注意力为例' and noted the generalization — strengthened the §6.2 closing caveat to make the additive-only scope explicit (names WY for DeltaNet, ∏α for GLA/Mamba-2).
rounds.confirmed_correct: linear-attention associativity + matrix state S_t=S_{t-1}+φ(k)v^T; SSM ZOH discretization Ā=exp(ΔA) + Mamba selectivity (B,C,Δ data-dependent, A structured-fixed); SSD M_ts=C_t(∏Ā_r)B̄_s 1-semiseparable ≡ structured masked linear attention (not softmax); delta-rule online-LSQ derivation S_t=S_{t-1}(I-β k k^T)+β v k^T; Gated DeltaNet α_t decay + β_t write — all independently re-derived correct.

real_issues_caught: §A note over-strong: claimed delta == additive 'ONLY when keys pairwise-orthogonal'. The precise condition is the erase term vanishing each step (S_{t-1}k_t=0); orthonormal keys + β=1 is a SUFFICIENT not necessary condition. Fixed both §A spots (inline comment + 💡 note).

block_topk_attention latent bug: the block representative score used mean over a -inf-padded view, so for L not divisible by `block` the last (partly-padded) block scored -inf and was never selectable (real tokens silently masked). Demo avoided it with L=12; fixed to a masked block-mean (pad scores 0, divide by real-column count) so any L is correct.
rounds.confirmed_correct: linear_attn_chunkwise is EXACTLY equal to linear_attn_recurrent for all L incl. ragged last chunk — self-inclusive convention (recurrent writes S before reading o_t; chunkwise tril includes the diagonal) and inter uses pre-chunk state: no off-by-one, no double-count. delta_rule_recurrent implements S(I-βkk^T)+β v k^T correctly.

rounds.notes: All fine: FlashAttention = exact softmax IO-opt (still O(L²) FLOPs, not linear); NSA three branches (compress+select+window, natively trainable, hardware-aligned); MoBA MoE-route-to-top-k-blocks vs NSA fixed three-branch; selective SSM can't FFT (time-varying kernel) → selective scan / SSD; DeltaNet ∏(I-βkk^T) parallelized via WY representation; hybrid ~1:5–1:7 full-attention ratio + Hymba head-level + not-constant-memory (full-attn layers keep O(L) KV).

fix_summary: (#60, CONFIRMED) softmax denominator 'sum exp >= 1' only holds after max-subtraction numerical stabilization, not for the raw formula (sum exp > 0 always, but no >=1 lower bound pre-shift) — §2.3 corrected.

(#61, CONFIRMED) S2.2/S6's outer-product order S=sum phi(k)v^T conflicts with S5 DeltaNet's transposed convention S=...+vk^T (masked by every demo setting d_k=d_v) — added an explicit convention note where S is first defined in S2.2 and again where DeltaNet's update is introduced in S5.1; did not rewrite either section's math (kept both internally self-consistent, doc-only fix).

(#62, CONFIRMED) 'SSM <=> 1-semiseparable matrix M' corrected to N-semiseparable (N = SSM state dim, e.g. Mamba's 64/128; rank<=1 '1-semiseparable' is only the degenerate N=1 case) — fixed consistently at TL;DR item 4, the S4.1 SSD callout, and Q13's answer.

(#63, CONFIRMED) Mamba-1 vs Mamba-2 'algorithmically equivalent, differs only scan vs matmul' narrowed: Mamba-2 also restricts A to scalar decay a_t*I (stronger than Mamba-1's per-channel diagonal A), so the genuine equivalence is the 3 eval-paths (scan/chunkwise/quadratic) of the SAME (Mamba-2-restricted) SSD layer, not Mamba-1 vs Mamba-2 as models — fixed at S4.2 interview-punchline and Q14.

(#64, CONFIRMED) S7.5 table 'training' cell for Longformer/BigBird corrected: they DO apply their sparse pattern during (continued) pretraining (e.g. Longformer continues MLM from RoBERTa), not only at fine-tuning; the real distinction from NSA is from-random-init vs continued-pretraining sparse training, not pretrain-vs-finetune — table cell shortened + explanatory footnote callout added.

(#65, CONFIRMED) S9.1: keeping even one full-attention layer in a hybrid keeps the model's ASYMPTOTIC time complexity at O(L^2) (that layer's quadratic term still dominates for large L) — hybrids cut the constant factor, not the complexity class; corrected to match the already-correct §8.2 KV-cache caveat.

(#66, NEEDS_NUANCE) RetNet's positional info was framed as pure scalar decay gamma^(t-s); added that RetNet's original formula also applies a complex rotation Theta_n=e^{i n theta} to Q/K (xPos/RoPE-style), so the full factor is gamma^(n-m) e^{i(n-m)theta} — noted at both S2.4 (brief) and S10's RoPE-relationship bullet (full).

(#67, CONFIRMED) 'linear attention is a finite-dimensional approximation of softmax' (S10 footgun #2) overgeneralized — only Performer/FAVOR+ explicitly approximates exp(q^Tk); ELU+1 (Katharopoulos) and RetNet/GLA use a different kernel entirely, not a softmax approximation (matches the doc's own §2.1 phrasing) — narrowed accordingly.

(#68, CONFIRMED) §A appendix code comment claimed 'S_{t-1}k_t=0 at every step' is the iff condition for delta-rule == additive; it is only SUFFICIENT for final-state equality (Delta_L = sum_t S_{t-1}^delta k_t k_t^T can vanish via cross-step cancellation without every term being zero) — fixed the inline comment and the matching §A read-the-numbers prose for item [e]. This snippet lives only in the .md's illustrative §A code block, not in code/linear_sparse_attention.py (whose own comments already said 'sufficient condition', unchanged).

(#59, NEEDS_NUANCE) S6.2's chunkwise derivation (and the S6.3/§A recurrent==chunkwise code check) silently use the UNNORMALIZED S_t=S_{t-1}+k_tv_t^T (no z_t denominator), while S2.2's boxed formula is the normalized definition (with z_t) — added a bridging sentence at S6.2 flagging this is the §2.3 unnormalized variant and noting how z_t could be carried through chunkwise if exact normalization were wanted.

(#69, NEEDS_NUANCE -> resolved by live verification) the References claim DeepSeek-V3.2/DSA has 'no independent arXiv paper' is now outdated: web search confirmed DeepSeek-AI published arXiv 2512.02556 'DeepSeek-V3.2: Pushing the Frontier of Open Large Language Models' (2025-12-02), which itself documents the DSA/lightning-indexer mechanism — reference entry updated with the arXiv id.
